events.title: Embargo Act Enforcement Expanded
events.description: Actually on December 22, 1807, the U.S. Congress passed the Embargo Act, signed by President Thomas Jefferson, which prohibited American ships from trading at foreign ports in response to British and French interference with American neutral shipping during the Napoleonic Wars.
events.significance: The embargo severely damaged the American economy, particularly New England commerce, and became a notable example of the limits of economic coercion as foreign policy; it was repealed in 1809.

events.title: Sherman Captures Savannah
events.description: Union General William T. Sherman telegraphed President Abraham Lincoln offering the city of Savannah, Georgia, as a Christmas gift after completing his March to the Sea, as Confederate forces had evacuated the city.
events.significance: The capture of Savannah demonstrated the Union's ability to wage total war through the Confederate heartland, crippled Southern infrastructure and morale, and hastened the end of the American Civil War.

events.title: Dreyfus Convicted of Treason
events.description: French Army officer Alfred Dreyfus, a Jewish captain, was wrongly convicted of treason by a military court-martial for allegedly passing secrets to Germany and was sentenced to life imprisonment on Devil's Island.
events.significance: The Dreyfus Affair divided French society, exposed deep antisemitism and institutional corruption, and became a landmark case in debates about justice, civil liberties, and the role of the press, notably prompted by Emile Zola's 'J'accuse'.

events.title: Ceausescu Regime Falls in Romania
events.description: Romanian dictator Nicolae Ceausescu and his wife Elena fled Bucharest by helicopter as mass protests overwhelmed his government; they were captured later that day and executed on December 25.
events.significance: The Romanian Revolution was the only violent overthrow of a Communist regime in Eastern Europe during the 1989 revolutions, ending more than two decades of repressive rule.

events.title: Lech Walesa Sworn In as President of Poland
events.description: Lech Walesa, co-founder of the Solidarity movement and Nobel Peace Prize laureate, was inaugurated as the first democratically elected President of Poland since World War II.
events.significance: His presidency symbolized Poland's peaceful transition from communist rule to democracy and marked a key milestone in the end of the Cold War in Eastern Europe.
